A084189.proof: digits >= 4 palindromic primes have odd length; product has exactly a+b digits (even); even-length palindrome divisible by 11. Lean a084189.

A225004.proof: d(nm)/d(n) = prod (a+x+1)/(a+1); a factor with x > a is >= 2. Lean exponents_le (product inequality only; divisor-count formula classical).

A340896.proof: d(n^2)/d(n) = prod (2a+1)/(a+1) >= 9/4 when two or more primes. Paper only, numeric check n <= 150.

A058383.proof: converse direction proved on paper; no other solution x <= 1e10

A276674.proof: x - lambda(x) even and positive excludes x = 1, 2 and odd prime powers; otherwise lambda(x) <= x/2 (even x: lambda <= phi <= x/2; odd x with two primes: lambda <= phi/2). Paper only, numeric check x <= 1e6.
